implementation_notes: Default C++ realization where the log is the broker: the consumer group plus committed offset is the durable position and the log's retention is the backlog store. Prefer it when the same C++ service both publishes and consumes events, since librdkafka's C and C++ APIs share configuration and semantics.
pitfalls: committing an unprocessed message loses it; committing after processing means the last batch is replayed on crash.
offsets.retention.minutes bounds the resume window; auto.offset.reset decides what happens after it expires.

variants.name: Paho C++ async_client with broker persistent session
variants.idiom_name: mqtt::async_client with a stable client id and clean session disabled
variants.implementation_notes: Where MQTT is the transport, the broker keeps the session and queues QoS 1/2 messages for the offline client id; the C++ client only declares the identity and acknowledges. Choose it for edge or device-style consumers where the broker is shared and per-client sessions are the natural unit of retention.
pitfalls: The C++ client object keeps its own in-flight state; a restart without the broker-side session loses QoS 2 bookkeeping.
Clean session is a broker-side session flag: changing the client id produces a brand-new subscription with an empty backlog.
